read.thesis: Premium card franchise reports record $10B net card fees (+18%) and 2026 guidance of 9-10% revenue and $17.30-17.90 EPS, with credit flat and VCE ratio rising to ~44%, but no supply-side capacity signal since it is a spend-led model.

triggers.label: Net card fees +18% to $10B
triggers.quote: Net card fee grew at 18% and reached a record of $10 billion for the year.

triggers.label: 2026 revenue +9-10%, EPS $17.30-17.90
triggers.quote: we expect 2026 revenue growth of 9% to 10% and EPS of $17.30 to $17.90.

triggers.label: Competition intensifying in SMB and consumer
triggers.quote: the competitive dynamic in consumer is as tough as it's ever been.

triggers.label: Platinum travel bookings up 30%
triggers.quote: We had an uptick of 30% in our travel bookings in the fourth quarter.

guidance.quote: we expect 2026 revenue growth of 9% to 10% and EPS of $17.30 to $17.90.
In 2026, we expect the VCE to revenue ratio to be around 44%.
In 2026, we expect operating expenses to grow in the mid-single digits.
We expect marketing expense to be up in the low single digits in 2026.
we expect to increase our quarterly dividend by 16% to 95¢ per share.

red_flags.label: Marketing and VCE spend rising to sustain growth; VCE ratio stepped up to 45%
red_flags.quote: The VCE ratio stepped up from earlier in the year as we expected driven by the investment we made in the value propositions of our US platinum cards.

red_flags.label: Middle-market SMB spend slowing
red_flags.quote: middle market is where you see a little bit of the slowdown.

evasions.quote: I wouldn't focus too much. I mean, if you look at it sequentially, it's a little bit down.

evasions.topic: Upside from credit and where excess returns go
evasions.quote: there will be certainly movements between the lines as the year progresses.
